around.headline: Ransom set but no call ever came — motive still a mystery in Bengaluru boy's murder
around.summary: Police are digging deeper into what drove a UK-returned MTech graduate to allegedly plot a boy's abduction and murder, since a Rs 1.5 crore ransom was fixed but the family never received a single call demanding it, per The Times of India and Deccan Herald. If you ever get an unexpected ransom or extortion call, don't negotiate alone — call 112 and let police manage contact.
around.source: The Times of India, Deccan Herald

around.headline: Man arrested for allegedly attempting murder with a dagger in Jayanagar
around.summary: Police arrested a man accused of attacking someone with a dagger in Jayanagar, per ThePrint, in a city that's seen a cluster of violent-crime arrests this weekend. In any assault in progress, 112 remains the fastest route to police response in Bengaluru.

around.headline: Civic body orders urgent repairs at Gunjur and Varthur junctions as parking violations hit a record
around.summary: Bengaluru's east zone civic chief has ordered immediate pothole repairs at the Gunjur and Varthur junctions, and NDTV separately flagged urgent repair needs on a heavily congested stretch, even as traffic police report a record 10.99 lakh wrong-parking cases booked this year, per The New Indian Express, NDTV and The Hindu. Expect construction-related slowdowns if your commute runs through Varthur or Sarjapur Road this week.
around.source: The New Indian Express, NDTV, The Hindu

around.headline: Voter-roll revision flags disproportionately high deletions in Bengaluru
around.summary: The ongoing Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls has cut names in Bengaluru at a disproportionately high rate, with 12 assembly seats seeing deletions cross 10 times the usual margin, even as Delhi's sitting and former chief ministers received similar SIR notices, per The Hindu. If you're a Bengaluru voter, check the draft roll on the CEO Karnataka site now to confirm your name hasn't been dropped.

around.headline: Lokayukta orders probe into poor-quality shoes supplied to government school students
around.summary: Karnataka's Lokayukta has ordered an inquiry into substandard shoes supplied to government school children after complaints about their quality, per TOI Bengaluru. Parents of affected students should hold on to any supply slips or receipts in case a replacement process follows.

around.headline: Tata Trusts declares Tata Sons board vote on Chandrasekaran's reappointment 'void ab initio'
around.summary: Tata Trusts has rejected the Tata Sons board's reappointment of N Chandrasekaran as chairman, calling the vote invalid from the outset in an escalating governance standoff atop India's largest business house, per The Hindu. The dispute touches Tata Group firms — from TCS to Tata Motors — where many Bengaluru employees, vendors and investors have a stake.

street_smart.title: You check the draft electoral roll during Bengaluru's ongoing voter-list revision (SIR) and find your name has been deleted, even though you've voted from this address for years — like the disproportionately high deletions flagged today across 12 city assembly seats. The correction window closes soon. What do you do?
street_smart.based_on: Today's real report: the ongoing Special Intensive Revision found deletions in Bengaluru disproportionately high, with 12 assembly seats crossing 10 times the usual margin, alongside Delhi's CM and former CM getting similar SIR notices (The Hindu). A wrongful voter-roll deletion scenario hasn't been used as a street-smart topic in the last three weeks.
street_smart.situation: You're fairly sure it's a clerical mix-up, not a real change in your eligibility, but you're also busy and the deadline to fix it isn't widely publicised.

choices.text: File a claim with your Booth Level Officer (BLO) or on the CEO Karnataka portal right away, attaching proof of address and your old voter ID, and keep the acknowledgment/receipt number.
choices.feedback: Correct. A formal claim creates the legal record election officials need to restore your entry, and the acknowledgment number is your proof if it doesn't get fixed in time — this is the only path that actually reverses a deletion before the roll is finalised.

choices.text: Assume it's a routine glitch that will sort itself out by election day, and take no action for now.
choices.feedback: This is the trap. SIR deletions become final once the revision window closes — 'it'll fix itself' is exactly the assumption behind today's spike in wrongful deletions, and by election day it's too late to file anything.

choices.text: Post about it on social media and call your local corporator's office to complain, without filing the formal objection.
choices.feedback: Risky. Public pressure might get attention, but it doesn't create the documented claim election officials are required to act on — without a filed form and receipt number, there's no paper trail forcing a fix before the deadline.

choices.text: Apply as a brand-new voter instead of trying to fix the deletion of your existing entry.
choices.feedback: Risky. A fresh application is a slower, separate process that can get flagged as a duplicate against your old (deleted) entry, and it may not clear in time — contesting the wrongful deletion directly is faster and cleaner.

takeaways: Check your name on the draft SIR roll now at ceo.karnataka.gov.in using your EPIC number — don't wait for a notice to arrive.
If deleted or details are wrong, file the correction/claim form with your BLO before the published cutoff, and always keep the acknowledgment slip as proof.
The national Voter Helpline (1950) can confirm your registration status and guide you to the right form if you're unsure where you stand.

quiz.question: Today's report says voter-roll deletions during the ongoing SIR were disproportionately high in Bengaluru, with how many assembly seats crossing 10 times the usual deletion margin?
quiz.why: A spike that large in a single revision cycle is what prompted scrutiny of the process, alongside similar SIR notices going out to Delhi's sitting and former chief ministers.

quiz.question: Karnataka's Lokayukta ordered a probe this week into poor-quality what, supplied to government school students?
quiz.why: The probe follows complaints about substandard material in shoes distributed under a state supply scheme.

quiz.question: Tata Trusts declared a Tata Sons board vote 'void ab initio' this week, rejecting the reappointment of whom as chairman?
quiz.why: Tata Trusts holds roughly two-thirds of Tata Sons, giving it outsized say over such board decisions — hence its ability to contest the vote's validity.

quiz.question: What is India's national, toll-free helpline number for checking your voter registration status or reporting electoral roll errors?
quiz.why: 1950 is run by the Election Commission and works across states, distinct from police (100), ambulance (108) and the anti-corruption vigilance helpline (1064).

quiz.question: Sunlight exposure on skin primarily helps the body synthesize which vitamin?
quiz.why: UVB rays trigger a reaction in skin cells that converts a cholesterol derivative into vitamin D3, which the liver and kidneys then activate.
